approach: One rule in athena-git: `Git::own_origin_url(remote)` refuses any remote name but `origin`, requires `git remote get-url --all origin` and `git remote get-url --push --all origin` to each list exactly one URL, and requires both to name the same repository. `Git::push_branch` and `Git::push_if_remote_at` call it first. In gh/remote.rs, `guard_origin_write(git, name)` wraps it and is called first in `GitRemote::push`, `replace` and `delete_branch`; reads stay unguarded. The pull-request side reads origin through the checked read plus a host check: `own_origin_repository(git)` = `own_origin_url` then `GhClient::origin_repository` (https, authority host equals github.com, client.rs:1026-1039), not the loose `parse_remote` (client.rs:1196 finds the host anywhere in the string). `Athena::land_pr` (landing.rs:865-867) and `Athena::github_repository` (early.rs:363-366) use it. Round 3 findings 1 and 2: I searched the callers and tests of `Athena::land_pr` myself (results in dependents). Only three call sites exist; no test reaches the changed origin read except the new ones, and the earlier claim that tests/drain.rs reaches land_pr was wrong (`PrLander` is never built in a test). The one real behavior change is that `land_pr` now refuses `ssh://github.com/...` and scp-style origins that `parse_remote` accepted (tests.rs:1191-1192 pin `parse_remote` itself, which does not change).

decisions.choice: Put the URL check in `athena_git::Git::own_origin_url` (athena-git/src/lib.rs) and have remote.rs `guard_origin_write` call it.
decisions.reason: athena-core depends on athena-git, not the reverse. The records writer pushes through `Git::push_branch`/`push_if_remote_at` (records_branch.rs:401-459), which GitRemote never sees. One implementation covers both paths; criterion 2 names both files.

rejected.why: Records pushes (append_to_remote from attribution.rs:785, gh/records.rs:156 and 365, reconcile.rs:746 and 841, records_import.rs:206) could still push to any named remote.

rejected.option: Duplicate the check in core and git
rejected.why: Two copies of a URL-identity rule can drift.

decisions.choice: Refuse when `get-url --all` or `get-url --push --all` lists more than one URL, or when the two name different repositories. Error text never echoes a URL. The conditions are tested separately: (a) two push URLs both naming the origin's own repository (only the count check refuses); (b) two fetch URLs and no push URL; (c) one push URL on another repository (only the same-repository check refuses).
decisions.reason: A push goes to every push URL (else the fetch URLs). `get-url --push --all` falls back to the fetch URLs, so one pair of reads covers both. `git remote set-url --add --push` on a remote with no pushurl adds one URL (a mismatch, not a double); a real double needs `git config --add remote.origin.pushurl <url>` run twice, and the test asserts `get-url --push --all` prints two lines before calling the guard so a fixture that is not a double fails loudly. client.rs:1194-1195 says URLs are not echoed because they may carry a credential.

rejected.option: Build the double with `git remote set-url --add --push`
rejected.why: It yields one push URL on another repository, which the same-repository check refuses; removing the count check would go unnoticed.
It returns the first URL only.

decisions.choice: Normalisation for the same-repository comparison: rewrite the scp colon to a slash only when the URL has no `scheme://`; keep an explicit port as part of the host; strip userinfo, a trailing slash and `.git`; lower-case the host only; compare the path case-sensitively.
decisions.reason: Rewriting the colon after stripping the scheme would turn `https://github.com:443/o/r` into `github.com/443/o/r`. Path-case and port-presence differences are refused on purpose: both fail closed (an error, never an extra write), and local paths are case-sensitive. Unit tests pin this.

rejected.option: Use parse_remote owner/name for the comparison
rejected.why: Local-path origins (every test) are not GitHub URLs and parse_remote rejects them.

decisions.choice: `own_origin_repository(git)` returns `(HOST.to_string(), owner/name)` from `own_origin_url(OWN_REMOTE)` followed by `GhClient::origin_repository(&url)`; anything else is an error with no URL echoed. `Athena::land_pr` uses it in place of `get-url` + `parse_remote`. The change is accepted to refuse `ssh://github.com/...` and `github.com:o/r` origins in land_pr, which parse_remote accepted.
decisions.reason: parse_remote does `url.find(HOST)` and checks neither scheme nor host, so `https://example.com/github.com/owner/repo` parses as owner/repo; land_pr would push to example.com and send open, merge and close calls to GitHub owner/repo, the upstream case OLY-B-BND-01 forbids. early.rs:329-338 already treats only https github.com as a GitHub origin (an ssh origin skips the CI push today), so land_pr and the early path would otherwise disagree. The system facts state that SSH remotes are refused at admission; I searched admission.rs, host_rules.rs and reconcile.rs for 'ssh' and found no code that does it, so that fact rests on the user's request, not on code I read. Callers of `Athena::land_pr`, all searched: commands.rs:286, drain.rs:3483 (PrLander, built only at drain.rs:4281 by `RealSteps::live`, called from commands.rs:346 and 371), gh/tests.rs:4909 (stops at 'has no verification', landing.rs:857, before the origin read at 865). No test reaches the origin read with a real or fake origin, so no existing test changes.

rejected.option: Keep parse_remote after the checked read
rejected.why: Accepts a non-GitHub host whose path contains github.com, so PR calls could target a repository that is not origin.
`GhClient::origin_repository` already is the strict reader; reuse it.

rejected.option: Teach own_origin_repository to accept ssh and scp GitHub forms
rejected.why: A second host parser to keep in step; early.rs and the CI read already use https only, and the system facts say SSH remotes are not supported.

decisions.choice: The guard allows exactly the name `origin` and has no list of allowed remotes.
decisions.reason: The rule is 'the repo's own origin'; every production caller passes the literal origin (landing.rs:865, early.rs:374-377 and 458-461, reconcile.rs:403, attribution.rs:510 DEFAULT_REMOTE, cli main.rs:1751, test_support.rs:620-645).

rejected.option: A config key listing allowed remotes
rejected.why: Touches athena.toml or defaults.toml (out of scope) and would let a setting widen the boundary.

decisions.choice: Narrow the land_pr ordering test to what it can show: `land_pr_builds_the_remote_and_sink_only_after_the_checked_origin_read` asserts on landing.rs text that `own_origin_repository(` comes before `GitRemote {` and before `GitLandingRecords::for_remote`. It claims ordering only.
decisions.reason: land_pr runs `self.reconcile` at landing.rs:842 before the origin read (865); reconcile (reconcile.rs:402-412) can write records through the git-level guard, which the athena-git twin tests show.

rejected.option: Build a verified job and call Athena::land_pr with no origin
rejected.why: Heavy setup (a verified job record, a fingerprint, a branch) for a property the first line of the origin read decides; the helper tests and the guard rechecks show the behavior.

decisions.choice: Show the early.rs change with a doubled GitHub origin built as a real double (two `remote.origin.pushurl` values, the first equal to the origin's own URL, the second another URL) plus a mismatched-single-push-URL case, with the EarlyFake installed and a single-URL GitHub control. Tell the two skip reasons apart: `push_ci_branch` prints 'CI branch push is skipped because origin has more than one URL or names two repositories' when origin exists but `own_origin_url` refuses, and keeps 'there is no GitHub origin' (early.rs:389) for no origin or a non-GitHub origin.
decisions.reason: github_repository already returns None for a local path (early.rs:329-338), so only a doubled GitHub origin separates the new read from the old. The control proves the fake is reachable. The old line would claim there is no GitHub origin when one exists and was refused. Existing assertions on the old line (run/tests.rs:1104 and 5872, a no-origin case) keep their meaning. `delete_ci_branch` and `early_pr` stay silent as today.

rejected.option: Leave the single 'no GitHub origin' line
rejected.why: Misleads the user about why the push was skipped.

decisions.choice: Record as a known coverage change that `checkpoint_write_failure_keeps_verdict` (attribution.rs:1690-1707) and `check_attribution_push_failure_keeps_the_verdict` (cli tests/binary.rs:631-660) now hit the guard instead of a failing git push. Restore the git-push-fails path with a new athena-git test: a single-URL bare origin whose `hooks/pre-receive` exits 1 (mode 0o755). The control (no hook) runs through `push_branch` and `push_if_remote_at` and returns Ok; with the hook, each returns `GitError::Failed` whose stderr contains git's hook-declined text, and the test fails if the error is `GitError::Refused`; refs unchanged.
decisions.reason: Asserting only Err cannot tell git's rejection from a wrong guard refusal. Matching on the variant and text does. Root does not bypass a hook; `Git::isolated` sets `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` through `-c` on the caller's git (lib.rs:190) and git does not hand that to the local receive-pack, so the bare repo's hook runs. If the hook did not run, the with-hook push would succeed and the test would fail rather than pass silently.

rejected.why: A wrongly strict guard also returns Err.

decisions.reason: They only read; their record writes go through the guarded push functions; rebase_job_branch 'never pushes' (landing.rs:754). None is a deliverable.

rejected.why: Not deliverables; a read is not publishing.

ScriptRunner is declared in a nested module (tests.rs:4794, after `mod stacked` at 4320), so the test that uses it sits in that module.

rejected.why: It would pass without the change.

risks.risk: A user whose origin has a push URL on another host or repository (a fork-style setup) is now refused; before, Athena pushed there.
risks.mitigation: This is the rule being enforced. Same-repo URL variants (https fetch, scp-style push, credentials, `.git`, trailing slash) are allowed; the refusal text says which condition failed without echoing a URL.

risks.risk: False refusals from strict normalisation (path case differs, explicit port on one URL only) and from refusing two identical push URLs.
risks.mitigation: All fail closed (an error, never an extra write); stated as intended and pinned by unit tests.

risks.risk: land_pr now refuses an origin that parse_remote accepted: `ssh://github.com/o/r`, `github.com:o/r`, or a non-GitHub host whose text contains github.com. A user with an ssh GitHub origin can push through git today and would now get an error from `athena land --pr`.
risks.mitigation: I searched all callers and tests: Athena::land_pr is reached only from commands.rs:286, drain.rs:3483 (never built in a test) and gh/tests.rs:4909 (stops earlier), so no existing test changes. The non-GitHub-host case could send host calls to a repository that is not origin. The ssh and scp refusal matches early.rs, which already treats only https github.com as a GitHub origin, and the system facts say SSH remotes are not supported; I found no admission code that enforces that. The error says the origin must be an https github.com URL and echoes no URL, and the CHANGELOG line states it.

risks.risk: The two pushurl fixtures (attribution.rs:1690-1707, cli tests/binary.rs:631-660) change from a git failure to a guard refusal.
risks.mitigation: Their assertions still hold; the athena-git hook test keeps git's own push failure covered (GitError::Failed); recorded as a known coverage change.

risks.risk: The `git config --add remote.origin.pushurl` double depends on git's output for `get-url --push --all`.
risks.mitigation: The test asserts two output lines (first equal to the fetch URL) before calling the guard, so a fixture that is not a double fails instead of passing on the wrong check.

risks.risk: Admission reads an added line holding the userinfo character as an address, and the boundary scan fails on banned words.
risks.mitigation: Use `'\u{40}'` in source (as client.rs:1030-1034 does), build test URLs without a literal credential, reuse the existing `concat!` in remote.rs for the pinned-push flag name, and run `cargo test -p xtask --test policy`.

risks.risk: gh/tests.rs is very large; `set_up()` and the early seam are thread-local, and ScriptRunner lives in a nested module.
risks.mitigation: Hold the `early_seam::Guard` in a local until the end of the test (as run_pin_tests.rs:425 and 433 do); put ScriptRunner-based tests in its module.

risks.risk: The land_pr ordering test is a source-text check and cannot show that reconcile (landing.rs:842, earlier) writes nothing.
risks.mitigation: It claims ordering only; enforcement is the recheck in GitRemote and Git, shown by the criterion 3 and 4 tests and the athena-git twin.

risks.risk: The hook test depends on the hook being executable and run by git in the temp bare repo.
risks.mitigation: Mode 0o755; the no-hook control goes through the same two push functions, and the with-hook case must return GitError::Failed with the hook-declined text, so a hook that does not run fails the test.

demonstrations.method: `git_remote_refuses_writes_to_any_remote_but_origin` builds a temp repo (`Git::isolated`, as at gh/tests.rs:2680-2703) with two bare repos as remotes `origin` and `upstream`, one commit, and a seed branch pushed to both with raw `git.run(["push", ...])`. Control, same user and environment: a raw `git push upstream` of a new branch succeeds and `ls-remote --heads upstream` is the baseline. Then `GitRemote { git, name: "upstream" }` `push`, `replace(branch, new, seed)` and `delete_branch(seed)` each return Err and upstream's refs equal the baseline; a third remote `mirror` is refused the same way. The same three calls on `GitRemote { name: "origin" }` succeed and origin's refs show the pushed, replaced and deleted branches. A twin test in athena-git/src/lib.rs does the same through `Git::push_branch` and `Git::push_if_remote_at`. Also run `cargo test -p athena-git`.
demonstrations.observes: The control push to upstream lands (so it is possible without the guard), every guarded write to upstream is an error with refs unchanged, and the same writes to origin succeed.
demonstrations.fails_without: Removing `guard_origin_write` from `GitRemote::push` lets the push to `upstream` land, so the is_err and unchanged-refs assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `GitRemote::push`/`replace`/`delete_branch` (remote.rs:52-79) and `Git::push_branch`/`push_if_remote_at` (athena-git lib.rs:384, 432); real git over temp bare repos, no fake; fixture style exists (gh/tests.rs:2680-2752). The tests and the guard are added by plan steps 2 to 6. The guard runs before any git push is spawned.

demonstrations.method: Tests in gh/tests.rs and athena-git. (a) `git_remote_with_no_origin_refuses_and_writes_nothing`: only `upstream`; `GitRemote{name:"origin"}` push/replace/delete_branch each Err; upstream refs unchanged. (b1) `git_remote_refuses_a_doubled_push_url`: origin accepts a push (control); then `git config --add remote.origin.pushurl <origin's own URL>` twice; the test asserts `git remote get-url --push --all origin` prints two lines and the first equals the fetch URL; push/replace/delete_branch Err and the bare is unchanged (only the count check can refuse). (b2) same with the second push URL on another bare: Err and both bares unchanged. (b3) `git_remote_refuses_a_doubled_fetch_url`: `git config --add remote.origin.url <second bare>` (two fetch URLs, no push URL); the test asserts `get-url --push --all` prints two lines; push Err, both bares unchanged. (c) `git_remote_refuses_a_push_url_naming_another_repository`: one `remote.origin.pushurl` on another bare; Err, unchanged (only the same-repository check can refuse). (d) `origin_repository_reads_only_the_parsed_owner_and_repo`: `own_origin_repository(git)` returns `example/project` for `https://github.com/example/project.git`; Err for no origin; Err for a local-path origin; Err for a local path containing `github.com/o/r`; Err for `https://example.com/github.com/owner/repo`; Err for `ssh://github.com/example/project.git` (the accepted behavior change); Err for the https GitHub origin with a doubled push URL (real double as in b1) and with a push URL on another repo. A close_pr(9) ScriptRunner path check is kept in the module that defines ScriptRunner as a regression note only. (e) `a_local_path_origin_makes_no_host_or_remote_call`, `a_doubled_github_origin_makes_no_host_or_remote_call`, `a_mismatched_github_push_url_makes_no_host_or_remote_call`: an `Athena` from `code_health::tests::set_up()` with an `EarlyFake` (test_support.rs:275) in the early seam, guard held to the end. Control: single-URL `https://github.com/example/project.git` makes the fake record a push and an open_pr. Local-path, doubled (real double) and mismatched origins: `early_pr`, `push_ci_branch`, `delete_ci_branch` leave `calls` and `ci_calls` empty; with the top-level `Lines` Ui (gh/tests.rs:3504) the doubled case prints the 'more than one URL or names two repositories' line and not 'no GitHub origin', and the local-path case still prints 'no GitHub origin'. (f) `land_pr_builds_the_remote_and_sink_only_after_the_checked_origin_read`: ordering of `own_origin_repository(` before `GitRemote {` and `GitLandingRecords::for_remote` in landing.rs (ordering only). (g) athena-git unit tests: normalisation (https vs scp-style same repo accepted; other repo refused; explicit port equal to itself accepted, refused against portless; path-case difference refused) and the hook test (control through `push_branch` and `push_if_remote_at` returns Ok with no hook; with `pre-receive` exit 1 each returns `GitError::Failed` with git's hook-declined text, not `Refused`; refs unchanged). Also run `cargo test -p athena-git`.
demonstrations.observes: Every refusal case returns Err (or makes no call) and every ref listing is unchanged. The doubled cases are proven doubled by the two-line assertion. A single-URL https GitHub origin yields only the parsed owner/repo; a non-GitHub host, an ssh form or a local path yields none. The control makes the EarlyFake record calls, so empty calls in the other cases mean refusal.
demonstrations.fails_without: Removing only the 'exactly one line' check on `get-url --push --all` makes (b1) push to the same repository twice and fail its Err assertion, while (c) still passes; removing only the same-repository check makes (b2) and (c) fail while (b1) still passes; removing the host check in `own_origin_repository` makes the example.com/github.com, ssh and local-path cases yield a repository; without the checked read in `github_repository`, the doubled GitHub origin makes the EarlyFake record a push and an open_pr; without the distinct skip line, the doubled case prints 'no GitHub origin'.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `GitRemote` methods, `Git::own_origin_url`, `own_origin_repository`, `Athena::early_pr`/`push_ci_branch`/`delete_ci_branch` (early.rs:384-437, pub(crate), same crate; `with_ci_remote` takes the seam first at early.rs:369-373 but `github_repository` still reads git, which is what the doubled case tests). Fixtures: real temp bare repos; `EarlyFake` injected through `gh::early_seam::install` (gh/mod.rs:99, exists, used at run_pin_tests.rs:425); `Lines` Ui exists (gh/tests.rs:3504); ScriptRunner exists (gh/tests.rs:4794). `own_origin_repository`, `Git::own_origin_url` and the tests are added by plan steps 2 to 6. No double holds the logic under test.
